gSASRec (RecSys 2023) directly supports testing the objective before adding architecture: sampled BCE can produce overconfident probabilities and poor separation among top-ranked items. It retains SASRec while increasing negatives and introducing generalized BCE calibration. Authors recommend k=256 negatives and calibration t=0.75; t=0 recovers BCE, while full calibration t=1 can converge more slowly. These findings make objective-induced weak separation plausible, but do not establish the cause in Electronics. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.07192), [official implementation](https://github.com/asash/gSASRec-pytorch/).

Multi-negative sampled softmax provides direct competition between the positive and sampled alternatives. Scoring cost grows approximately as O(BLKd), versus O(BLNd) for full-catalog scoring; the sequence encoder is unchanged. In-batch candidates enable efficient matrix multiplication but follow item frequency. RecSys 2025’s “Correcting the LogQ Correction” shows that conventional correction mishandles the always-present positive and proposes a refined estimator. A 2024 sampling comparison finds dataset-dependent tradeoffs: uniform sampling favored head-item performance, while popularity-based sampling improved balance at possible aggregate accuracy cost. [LogQ paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331), [sampling study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276).

Sampling bias and false negatives are separate problems; calibration does not identify unobserved positives. Earlier UFNRec uses teacher soft labels and consistency regularization for suspected false negatives, adding training overhead. [UFNRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116). Practical experimental recommendation: hold architecture fixed; compare single-negative BCE, multi-negative BCE, gBCE, and sampled softmax using identical negatives and GPU-time limits. Start with 16–64 negatives, then scale promising objectives. Exclude padding, target collisions, and known training-history positives; never consult held-out labels. Select by four-category macro validation HR@10.
